description.describe_ch: 著重整體環境規劃與設計：包括群體建築之規劃與設計；開放空間之探討。設計方法之強化：以既有設計方法論，檢討建築設計最佳化之可行性。強調規劃設計過程，包含規劃目標、資料收集、分析、調查和研究，引導獲得正確的規劃方法。設計題目由各組指導老師出題。
description.describe_eh: Focus on the integration urban issues with architecture design. Projects will include following subjects: Cluster building design.building preservation and renevation, urban and landscape design.Design methodologg will be emphatcaller  discussed in this years' design project. Each studio has it's own goals and design topics.

textBooks.tpb_book: 本課程鼓勵同學運用創意並透過實作培養學生的設計能力。因此並無固定之教科書。
textBooks.tpb_book_en: This class emphasize the cultivation of student's problem-solving. There is no textbook.

readings.tpc_book:
為鼓勵同學了解設計趨勢，接軌國際，同學必須閱讀設計網站得獎案例介紹連結如下
https://www.moe-idc.org/Competition

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
課堂要求
評圖簡報以電子檔呈現，頁數不限請以PDF格是呈現。
內容包含：(專題組別除外)
（一）、	計畫緣由
（二）、	基地位置及範圍
（三）、	基地及週邊現況環境分析
1.	自然環境分析
2.	圖底圖分析
3.	開放空間分析 (綠帶、公園、廣場、水文)
4.	交通網絡分析 (車行系統、人行系統、公共運輸、停車場)
5.	基地週邊量體樓層高度分佈狀況分析
6.	土地使用現況分析 (住商混合狀況、公共設施、文化產業網絡)
7.	各組老師規定項目
（四）、	案例分析 (至少兩個)
（五）、	計畫目標與空間需求
1.	發展議題、目標
2.	全區開放空間計畫、交通系統計畫
3.	都市設計方案、量體計畫、定性定量（依各組老師規定）
（六）、	建築設計方案(scale可依題目設計需求由指導老師另行規定)
1.	量體/屋頂配置圖，不得小於1/500或由指導老師規定 (含基地周圍道路及開放空間關係、出入口位置、人車動線、停車空間、各種景觀元素等)
2.	各層平面圖(含一樓配置)，原則1/200或由指導老師規定
3.	建築物入口、垂直水平動線、單元空間平面等
4.	各空間門窗、傢俱、地坪材料、高程、空間名稱皆須繪圖表達
5.	公共空間樓電梯、廁所皆須正確繪圖
6.	立面圖每棟至少兩向，原則1/200或由指導老師規定
7.	請繪製陰影、景觀元素等真實呈現環境與建築相互關係
8.	屋頂形式、屋突、平台、陽台、欄杆等須正確繪圖
9.	剖面圖自選兩向，原則1/200或由指導老師規定
10.	清楚表達空間大小上下水平等相互關係
11.	樑、板、柱、天花、外牆、基礎等構造關係須清楚正確表達
（七）、	模型
1.	設計全區基地模+量體或電腦建模擇一。
2.	其他草模、概念模 (依各組老師規定)。
＊以上報告書需作成PPT檔，評圖當天報告使用。並準備紙本一份當天使用。
評分重點：設計策略及合理性，應充分考慮議題及基地環境條件
（一）、	下列狀況列入課程委員會討論成績
        甲、	期中及期末評點名未到者不予評圖並列入課程委員會討論。
        乙、	期中評圖圖面、模型未繳任何一項列入課程委員會討論。
        丙、	評圖時採『唱名』不到者，不得參加評圖，列入課程委員會討論。
（二）、	當天評圖結束後，每位同學均需繳交『評圖筆記』，未繳交者，扣平時分數，並從嚴處理（A4直式，請自備紙張）。
（三）、	請注意服裝儀容，女士請著套裝，男士請著襯衫長褲，表現好的同學將酌量加分。
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Classroom Requirements

The presentation should be in electronic format, preferably in PDF, and there is no limit to the number of pages.

Content to include (except for special project groups):

(1) Project rationale.

(2) Location and scope of the site.

(3) Analysis of the site and its surrounding environment.

Natural environment analysis.
Analysis of site base maps.
Open space analysis (green areas, parks, squares, hydrology).
Traffic network analysis (vehicular and pedestrian systems, public transport, parking).
Analysis of the distribution of building heights around the site.
Analysis of land use (mixed-use, public facilities, cultural industry networks).
Other specific items set by the respective instructors.
(4) Case studies (at least two).

(5) Project objectives and spatial requirements.

Development issues and objectives.
Open space planning for the entire area.
Transportation system planning.
Urban design scheme.
Massing planning.
Qualitative and quantitative aspects (as specified by the respective instructors).
(6) Architectural design scheme (scale to be determined by the supervising instructor's requirements).

Site and roof plan, not smaller than 1/500 or as specified by the supervising instructor (including the relationship of the site to surrounding roads and open spaces, entrances and exits, circulation for vehicles and pedestrians, parking spaces, various landscape elements, etc.).
Floor plans for each level (including the ground floor layout), generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Building entrances, vertical and horizontal circulation, unit space plans, etc.
Drawings must clearly express space names, doors, windows, furniture, floor materials, elevations, and spatial names.
Elevators and restrooms in public spaces must be accurately drawn.
For facades, draw at least two elevations for each building, generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Please depict shadows, landscape elements, and the relationship between the environment and the buildings accurately.
Roof forms, projections, platforms, balconies, railings, etc., must be accurately drawn.
For sections, choose two directions, generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Clearly express relationships between space sizes, elevations, etc.
Structural relationships such as beams, slabs, columns, ceilings, exterior walls, foundations, etc., must be clearly and correctly expressed.
(7) Models.

Design the entire site model or a computer model (choose one).
Other rough models or concept models (as specified by the respective instructors).
All the above reports must be made into a PPT file and used for the presentation on the day of evaluation. Additionally, prepare a hard copy for use on that day.

Grading Focus: Design strategy and rationality, taking into full consideration the issues and site environmental conditions.

(1) The following situations will be discussed by the course committee and may result in a failing grade:

Those who are absent from the mid-term and final evaluations will not be evaluated.
Those who do not submit any drawings or models for the mid-term evaluation will be discussed by the course committee.
Those who are absent when their name is called during the evaluation will not be allowed to participate in the evaluation and will be discussed by the course committee.
(2) After the evaluation on that day, each student must submit "evaluation notes." Failure to do so will result in a deduction from the regular score and strict handling. Please prepare A4 portrait paper for this purpose.

(3) Please pay attention to your dress and appearance. Ladies should wear suits, and gentlemen should wear dress shirts and long pants. Students who perform well may receive extra points at the discretion of the instructors.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem: 準時是一個基本的自我要求，請務必遵照課堂上課的規定。
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en: Punctuality is a fundamental self-expectation. Please be sure to adhere to the class schedule and regulations.
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno:
1. 學生對於自己所繳交的作業有負全責的義務。
2. 學習過程須清楚標示圖面來源，以示學術誠信。
3. 嚴禁剽竊與抄襲，最重將會送課程委員會討論，並做出不及格之處置。
gradeRuleDescribe.ais_meno_en:
1. Academic Integrity Statement: Academic integrity is of utmost importance in this course. Any form of plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, or misrepresentation of another person's work constitutes a serious violation of academic ethics. All students must ensure that the assignments and projects they submit are their original work and adhere to proper citation standards, clearly attributing the use of external resources. If academic misconduct is detected, it will result in appropriate penalties, which may include the assignment or course being evaluated as failing.
  2. Course Policies: Assignments: All assignments must be completed independently and not through copying or collaborating with others. If collaboration is needed, it must be approved by the course instructor. Citations: Proper citation is required when using external resources, including text, images, videos, etc. Failure to cite properly will be considered plagiarism and will be subject to corresponding penalties. Violation Review: Serious cases of academic misconduct will be reviewed by the course instructor. Penalties: The consequences of academic misconduct are severe and may include but are not limited to assignment failure or course failure. Please note that adhering to academic integrity and course policies is the responsibility of every student. Please maintain a honest and upright attitude throughout your learning process to ensure the authenticity and value of your academic achievements.

（二）、	當天評圖結束後，每位同學均需繳交『評圖筆記』，未繳交者，扣平時分數，並從嚴處理（A4直式，請自備紙張）。
（三）、	請注意服裝儀容，女士請著套裝，男士請著襯衫長褲，表現好的同學將酌量加分。
policy.course_pol_en:
Classroom Requirements

The presentation should be in electronic format, preferably in PDF, and there is no limit to the number of pages.

Content to include (except for special project groups):

(1) Project rationale.

(2) Location and scope of the site.

(3) Analysis of the site and its surrounding environment.

Natural environment analysis.
Analysis of site base maps.
Open space analysis (green areas, parks, squares, hydrology).
Traffic network analysis (vehicular and pedestrian systems, public transport, parking).
Analysis of the distribution of building heights around the site.
Analysis of land use (mixed-use, public facilities, cultural industry networks).
Other specific items set by the respective instructors.
(4) Case studies (at least two).

(5) Project objectives and spatial requirements.

Development issues and objectives.
Open space planning for the entire area.
Transportation system planning.
Urban design scheme.
Massing planning.
Qualitative and quantitative aspects (as specified by the respective instructors).
(6) Architectural design scheme (scale to be determined by the supervising instructor's requirements).

Site and roof plan, not smaller than 1/500 or as specified by the supervising instructor (including the relationship of the site to surrounding roads and open spaces, entrances and exits, circulation for vehicles and pedestrians, parking spaces, various landscape elements, etc.).
Floor plans for each level (including the ground floor layout), generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Building entrances, vertical and horizontal circulation, unit space plans, etc.
Drawings must clearly express space names, doors, windows, furniture, floor materials, elevations, and spatial names.
Elevators and restrooms in public spaces must be accurately drawn.
For facades, draw at least two elevations for each building, generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Please depict shadows, landscape elements, and the relationship between the environment and the buildings accurately.
Roof forms, projections, platforms, balconies, railings, etc., must be accurately drawn.
For sections, choose two directions, generally at 1/200 or as specified by the supervising instructor.
Clearly express relationships between space sizes, elevations, etc.
Structural relationships such as beams, slabs, columns, ceilings, exterior walls, foundations, etc., must be clearly and correctly expressed.
(7) Models.

Design the entire site model or a computer model (choose one).
Other rough models or concept models (as specified by the respective instructors).
All the above reports must be made into a PPT file and used for the presentation on the day of evaluation. Additionally, prepare a hard copy for use on that day.

Grading Focus: Design strategy and rationality, taking into full consideration the issues and site environmental conditions.

(1) The following situations will be discussed by the course committee and may result in a failing grade:

Those who are absent from the mid-term and final evaluations will not be evaluated.
Those who do not submit any drawings or models for the mid-term evaluation will be discussed by the course committee.
Those who are absent when their name is called during the evaluation will not be allowed to participate in the evaluation and will be discussed by the course committee.
(2) After the evaluation on that day, each student must submit "evaluation notes." Failure to do so will result in a deduction from the regular score and strict handling. Please prepare A4 portrait paper for this purpose.

(3) Please pay attention to your dress and appearance. Ladies should wear suits, and gentlemen should wear dress shirts and long pants. Students who perform well may receive extra points at the discretion of the instructors.

policy.ais_meno_en:
1. Academic Integrity Statement: Academic integrity is of utmost importance in this course. Any form of plagiarism, unauthorized collaboration, or misrepresentation of another person's work constitutes a serious violation of academic ethics. All students must ensure that the assignments and projects they submit are their original work and adhere to proper citation standards, clearly attributing the use of external resources. If academic misconduct is detected, it will result in appropriate penalties, which may include the assignment or course being evaluated as failing.
  2. Course Policies: Assignments: All assignments must be completed independently and not through copying or collaborating with others. If collaboration is needed, it must be approved by the course instructor. Citations: Proper citation is required when using external resources, including text, images, videos, etc. Failure to cite properly will be considered plagiarism and will be subject to corresponding penalties. Violation Review: Serious cases of academic misconduct will be reviewed by the course instructor. Penalties: The consequences of academic misconduct are severe and may include but are not limited to assignment failure or course failure. Please note that adhering to academic integrity and course policies is the responsibility of every student. Please maintain a honest and upright attitude throughout your learning process to ensure the authenticity and value of your academic achievements.
